# Compiled 2020-03-10 by Alan Heays.
# 
# There are many laboratory studies of O2 photoabsorption, mostly
# available on the Mainz UV/VIS database. The cross section adopted here
# is compiled from several sources:
# 
# Wavelength(nm)  Reference                DOI
# 4-49            brion1979                10.1016/0368-2048(79)85032-X
# 49-103          holland1993              10.1016/0301-0104(93)80148-3
# 103-107.97      watanabe1956             10.1063/1.1743151
# 107.97-108.7    wu2005                   10.1016/j.elspec.2005.01.047
# 108.7-120.6     ogawa1975                10.1139/p75-236
# 120.6-122.5     dose1975                 10.1007/BF01421028
# 108.7-120.6     ogawa1975                10.1139/p75-236
# 115-179.22      lu2010                   10.1051/0004-6361/201013998
# 179.22-240      yoshino1983,yoshino1992  10.1016/0032-0633(83)90085-5,10.1016/0032-0633(92)90056-T
# 
# The photoionisation efficiency of holland1993 is used to compute a
# photoionisation/photodissociation cross section shortwards of the
# ionisation threshold.
# 
# The O2 cross section has been studied at high and low
# temperatures. The data compiled here is uniformly measured near room
# temperature.
# 
# The spectrum is likely well resolved at all wavelengths apart from an
# interval between 103 and 117nm.  The many absolute cross sections
# measured are in generally good agreement where they overlap, and a 15h%
# absolute uncertainty is a reasonable general assumption.
# 
# wavelength   photoabsorption photodissociation   photoionisation
